finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so nothing can be called too wide, too low or too high yet; this is a first build. Built totals for one injector fitted (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2025 Chevrolet Trax 1.2L about $332-$461 (2.5 hr, the maker's time for all three injectors); midsize 2021 Hyundai Sonata 2.5L about $259-$351 (1.5 hr); truck 2016 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 5.3L about $446-$773 (2.9-3.9 hr); luxury 2016 Cadillac Escalade 6.2L about $420-$771 (2.9-3.9 hr). A supportable range for one direct injector is therefore roughly $260-$775, and every labor figure in it is a manufacturer warranty time, which is the low end of what a shop bills, so real quotes will often be higher. How solid the labor times are: all four are manufacturer times for the example vehicle. The Hyundai 1.5 hr (Sonata) is the best fit: the bulletin prints it for 'Replace 1 GDI fuel injector'. The GM 2.9 hr (Silverado and Escalade) is printed for '1-4 injectors on first bank', so it also covers one injector. The economy figure is the weak one: no maker bulletin was found that prints a one-injector time for an economy car, so the Trax 2.5 is GM's time for the full set of three, taken from a table that prints no unit, in a bulletin for cars still in dealer stock, and it includes the fuel feed pipe and camshaft cover gasket work. A full-set time is a fair stand-in on a direct-injection engine, because the fuel rail comes off either way (Hyundai allows 1.5 hr for one injector and 1.3 hr for four), but it is not a stated one-injector time. Other makers' full-set times for small engines run from 0.7 hr (Jeep Renegade 1.3L) to 1.8 hr (Honda Fit), so the Trax figure is at the high end. No class has a shop-level upper time: the midsize and economy ranges are a single maker figure, and the truck and luxury 3.9 hr is our sum of GM's 2.9 hr and its maximum 1.0 hr diagnostic add-on. No trade-press or shop book time was found for any of the four vehicles. How solid the parts are: three of the four low ends (economy, midsize, luxury) are an online dealer's discounted price for the genuine injector, not an aftermarket price, so those parts ranges are narrower than a true aftermarket-to-list range. For the Sonata one new aftermarket injector was found (Standard FJ1608) but its price did not load clearly. For the Trax the priced part is 25206285, which the catalog shows as replaced by the 25207703 the bulletin names. The truck's genuine kit (12698484) is the one GM's bulletin names but the catalog page loaded lists it only for 2019-2021 trucks and does not state the quantity in the kit. What this file does not cover: all four examples are direct injection, because the only manufacturer bulletins found that print an injector time are for direct-injection engines; port injectors are usually cheaper and quicker and nothing reliable is said about them here. Some makers sell injectors only as a set (Honda: the 2015 Fit set of four lists at $1,640.85-$1,776.31 and the 2023 Accord Hybrid kit at $732.42), and Hyundai's latest bulletins for the Sonata's engine (2025 and 2026) call for all four injectors on affected cars, so a dealer quote may be for a set and several times the one-injector parts figure. European direct-injection cars (ConsumerAffairs shows $3,112-$3,350 for all injectors on a BMW 740i) are not priced here. Against the benchmarks: RepairPal's $768-$953 national average sits at the top of our truck and luxury totals and well above the two four-cylinder totals, and its parts figure ($464-$507) is three to eight times one genuine injector here ($61-$149 list), which suggests it prices more than one injector; Synchrony's $350-$850 brackets our totals; ConsumerAffairs gives $300 to over $4,000 for a single injector, which shows how wide this job runs. Confidence is low: the economy time is a full-set time, no class has a shop-level upper time, and three low parts prices are discounted genuine parts. Second attempt (2026-11-20): the economy and midsize examples were changed from the Honda Fit and Accord Hybrid, whose injectors are sold only as sets, to cars whose makers sell one injector. Held (2026-11-20, second attempt, reviewer): the only economy time is GM's figure for all three injectors on the Trax, printed with no unit and including fuel pipe and cam cover gasket work, so it is a cross-check and the economy hours are left empty. No maker prints a one-injector time for an economy car (GM, Hyundai, Kia, Honda, Mazda, Nissan and FCA small cars were checked). Midsize (2021 Sonata, Hyundai 1.5 hr for one injector), truck and luxury are complete. This job stays held and does not block the others.
extras: A quote usually adds diagnosis first (misfire or fuel-trim testing, an injector balance test; GM allows up to 1.0 hr for it and Honda 0.3 hr), and often: new seals, O-rings, clips or a one-time-use high-pressure fuel pipe where the maker requires them (Hyundai requires a new pipe and bolts; GM lists a fuel feed pipe, retainers and a camshaft cover gasket on the Trax), intake manifold gaskets when the manifold has to come off, an engine oil change if a leaking injector has thinned the oil with fuel, spark plugs fouled by the bad injector, injector coding or a relearn on some engines, shop supplies and sales tax. Shops often recommend replacing the whole bank or the full set at once, and on some cars the maker sells the injectors only as a set or calls for the full set, which multiplies the parts cost. Carbon cleaning of the intake valves on direct-injection engines is a separate service.
